MAKE SURE TO PAY FOR A PARKING ON THEIR WEBSITE BEFORE YOU COME. Pros: 
Great hiking trail through shaded forest and wetland. The terrain gets very rocky at times which can make it pretty challenging but the views are amazing. Bug spray is needed just like on all hikes, but shade makes sunscreen not necessary.  Not too much mud and the trail is mostly flat. There are a lot of alternative routes you can take to make your journey more interesting. 
Cons:
You must pay to access the trails and since it’s paid, the route is maintained very well. I personally like trails which have a more wild feel to them. This place also gets a lot of traction especially at noon due to rock climbing, so if you want to experience the silence of the forest, come at 8:30 (which is when it opens). Overall very positive experience, especially from the side trail routes.

August 2023 - park at the lower lot. The entrance to the trail is to the left of the information board (the right entrance is closed for construction to the trail).  Keep walking until buffalo crag lookout. For some reason the next part of the trail has that orange construction fence.  Ignore it and keep walking ahead to Crawford lake. The trail is maintained and lots of people were using it. A comfortable hike should take around 3 hours for a total of 11km.  This was my second time doing this hike.

This trail was marked closed about 1/4 into it (with a sign, but fencing was removed - and hikers were using it) and then totally closed about 3/4 of the way with many cut trees blocking it, so there we detoured to the lake. Before that last bit, the trail was beautiful and the terrain was wonderful - with lots of roots and rocks so you have to pay attention to where you step, and good elevation changes that weren’t too challenging but were worthy of a rest here and there. Kudos to the volunteers who created a lovely boardwalk/bridge spot with built-in benches. So grateful to friends of parks!

Make note, you must make a reservation time slot online at parkvisit.ca and it’s $6.50 per adult. Reservation is by license plate. Depending on if it’s busy or not, you can buy outside the gate on your phone and go in then. Trail was gorgeous, 10.2km round but we didn’t loop the lake as we’ve done it before. Take the side trails to the left on the first straight trail, lots of views of the valley. Also make note, when you get to the lookout point, the main trail is closed, but you can continue along the side trails marked blue, just go to the left pathway if you’re going from the main trail and it’s to the right of the lookout, it’ll take you around to the main trail. Keep in mind it is very rocky, and quite rugged terrain but as an experienced hiker it’s expected and not hard (also lots of steep cliffs as you hike so do not bring your kids). The lake was nice to hike to. You’ll see cool wood carved statues as you get to the lake, worth the long hike if you’re looking for some exercise. Also tons of bugs, put bug spray before if they like you lol.
